parentEmulator.title: Try it yourself — a practice copy of Edura
parentEmulator.missHint: Not that one — look for the control with the purple outline and press it.
parentEmulator.finishedBody: You can now follow your child, link your children, top up your wallet and pay from it, and you know exactly what you can and cannot see of their conversations. Your real account works the same way.
parentEmulator.sandboxNote: Everything above is practice — the data is invented, no real money moves, and nothing is saved to your account.

firstRun.title: Welcome — want to try it first?
firstRun.body: A short practice run on a copy of Edura: follow your child, link them to your account, top up your wallet and pay for a lesson — without spending anything or touching your account.
firstRun.reopenHint: You can reopen it any time from “Guided tour” in the menu.

screens.byFamilyCodeHint: Your child finds this code in their account under “Family Code”. Linking is instant.
screens.byEmailOrPhoneHint: You send a request, and your child approves it from their account.
screens.confirmBody: One lesson for {name}. Choose how to pay.
screens.insufficient: Your wallet balance is short — top it up or pay by card.
screens.readOnlyNotice: Read-only view. Opening this does not mark anything as read for your child.
screens.noReply: There is no reply box here — and there isn't one in the real product either.

welcome.title: Welcome — this is a practice copy of Edura
welcome.body: The screen below is Edura exactly as it is, filled with an invented family. Press whatever you like — nothing here touches your account.

children.title: Your children in one place
children.body: Every child linked to your account appears here with their name and grade. If you have more than one, you see them all from the same account.

record.title: And how each one is doing
record.body: Attendance rate and average grade. Both are worked out from your child's actual attendance and the grades their teacher entered — nobody types these in.

goChildren.title: First thing you must do: link your child
goChildren.body: Without a link, every screen in your account stays empty. Press “Children” in the menu.

twoWays.title: There are two ways to link
twoWays.body: By family code — which links instantly — or by email or phone, where you send a request and your child approves it.

byCode.title: Link by family code
byCode.body: Your child finds this code in their own account. Press “Link instantly”.

approved.title: A link has to be Approved
approved.body: A request that is still pending, or was rejected, or has been revoked gives you no access at all. Only “Approved” opens your child's data.

openWallet.title: Before you pay, look at your wallet

short.title: You only have 50 EGP
short.body: And the lesson is 120. Paying from the wallet is **all or nothing** — if the balance is short the whole payment is refused and no part of it is taken.

topUp.title: Top it up
topUp.body: Press “Top up”. For real it asks the amount and takes you to pay by card — top-ups are by card only, never from another wallet.

whichChild.title: The record tells you who you paid for
whichChild.body: Every payment line in your wallet carries the name of the child it was for. That is what lets you check your money when you have more than one.

notChildWallet.title: Your wallet is not your child's wallet
notChildWallet.body: They are two entirely separate balances. You pay from your own money and cannot spend your child's — and they cannot spend yours either.

openPay.title: Now let's pay
openPay.body: Press “Pay for a Lesson” in the menu.

pickLesson.title: Read the lesson before you pay
pickLesson.body: The teacher, the times, the centre and the price are all in front of you before you press anything.

fromWallet.title: Pay from your wallet
fromWallet.body: Press “Pay from my wallet”. If you would rather pay by card directly, that choice sits next to it.

paid.title: The lesson is active
paid.body: The money left your wallet, the lesson is paid for your child, and a new line appeared in your wallet history with their name on it.

openSafety.title: One important thing left: child safety

readOnly.title: Reading only — nothing more
readOnly.body: You can read your child's conversations with teachers, assistants and centre staff. **You cannot reply** and you cannot delete. And opening a conversation does not mark anything as read for them.

childKnows.title: And your child knows
childKnows.body: A clear notice appears in the conversation, for them and for the other person, saying a parent can see it. This is not surveillance — it is disclosed to both sides.

adultsOnly.title: Their chats with friends are not here
adultsOnly.body: You only see conversations with **adults**. And if your child is over 18 with a verified age, their conversations are entirely private and you cannot see them.

parentTour.title: A quick tour of Edura
parentTour.moreHint: On a phone: press “More” first — it's inside there.

welcome.title: Welcome to Edura 👋
welcome.body: This is where you follow your children and pay for them. The tour shows you the things you'll actually do — and it won't just say “this is your wallet”, it will show you how, step by step. You can skip it at any point.

linkChild.title: First: link your child
linkChild.body: Without a link, every screen in your account stays empty. There are two ways.

how.2: Ask your child for their family code — it's in their account under “Family Code”
how.3: Enter the code and press “Link instantly”
how.4: Or enter their email or phone and press “Send request” — then they approve it from their account

linkChild.note: A link has to be Approved. Pending, rejected or revoked gives you no access to your child's data at all.

progress.title: How to follow how your child is doing
progress.body: Their marks per subject and their overall level.

how.2: If you have more than one child, pick them from the bar at the top of the page
how.3: Look through the subjects, percentages and bands

progress.note: The pass mark is 50%. Grades are entered by the teacher — if one is wrong, speak to the teacher or the centre.

attendance.title: How to know whether your child attended
attendance.body: The daily question: did they actually go today?

how.2: Pick the child if you have more than one
how.3: At the top: present / late / absent
how.4: Below it, a coloured day map showing their consistency

attendance.note: If your child's group uses two check-ins, they must also check in at the hall door — without it the lesson is not counted as attended.

fees.title: How to see what you owe
fees.body: What's outstanding per child, and what has been paid.

how.2: See what's due per child and per group
how.3: This is where you find out what to pay before going to the payment screen

wallet.title: How to top up your wallet
wallet.body: Your own balance. Top it up once and pay for your children's lessons from it.

how.3: Enter the amount in pounds, confirm and pay by card

wallet.note: Your wallet is entirely separate from your child's — you pay from your own money and cannot spend theirs. And wallet payments are all or nothing: if the balance is short the whole payment is refused.

pay.title: How to pay for your child's lesson
pay.body: This is usually why you opened the account.

how.1: Press “Pay for a Lesson” in the menu
how.3: Pick the subject, then the group
how.4: Press “Pay for this lesson” — or “Pay monthly” for the whole month
how.5: Choose “Pay by card” or “Pay from my wallet”

pay.note: Your wallet history records the child's name next to every payment — that's what lets you check your money when you have more than one.

messages.title: How to message the teacher or the centre
messages.body: If you have a question, you can write directly.

how.3: Pick the name from the list

safety.title: How to see your child's conversations — and the limits
safety.body: You can read your child's conversations with teachers, assistants and centre staff.

how.3: Tap a conversation to read it

safety.note: Read-only: you cannot reply and cannot delete. Your child knows — a notice appears in the conversation for both sides. Opening it does not mark anything as read for them. Their chats with friends never appear here, and if they're over 18 with a verified age their conversations are entirely private.

notifications.title: How to get alerts
notifications.body: So you know the moment your child misses a class, a grade is recorded, or a payment goes through.

how.1: Press “Notifications” in the menu to read what happened
how.2: For alerts on your phone: open “Settings”
how.3: Find the push notifications section and press “Enable”
how.4: Your browser asks for permission — press “Allow”

practice.title: And if you'd rather try it first
practice.body: There's a full practice copy you can rehearse on without spending anything or touching your account.

how.2: It walks you through it: link a child, top up, pay for a lesson, and view conversations
how.3: All the data in it is invented

finish.title: That's it — your turn 🎉
finish.body: The tour is done. Start by linking your child from “Children” — that's what opens the rest of the account. And if you'd rather rehearse first, “Practice” is in the menu.
